bugs.creator: michaelchirico4
bugs.summary: Confusing behavior of quote= in print.table

comments.text:
I came to `quote=` trying to get distinction in the output between different "blank" inputs:

```
s = rep(c("", " ", "  "), each=1e5)
print(table(s))

# s
#                      
# 100000 100000 100000 
```

Not very useful!

`?print.table` shows us `quote=` as maybe helpful here, but here's the surprising output:

```
# s
#                            
# "100000" "100000" "100000" 
```

Not only does this not help us, it doesn't match the stated purpose of `quote=` in `?print.table`:

https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/blob/31340c871c7df54e45bfc7c4f49d09bb5806ec70/src/library/base/man/print.Rd#L36-L37

> `quote` - logical, indicating whether or not strings should be printed with surrounding quotes.

But here, the _strings_ have been left alone, while the _integer_ counts of values have been surrounded with quotes.
comments.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.text:
Amazing ... 
I do agree that the  `quote` argument as implemented is almost always useless.
I'm almost sure, I will not have used it ever.
Still, not all `"table"` objects need to be have produced by `table()` {or similar}, i.e., one *may* have tables with string entries.

In addition, what I *have* used quite frequently is  `print.table(<matrix>, zero.print = ".")`

which is *very* nice to make the console output much more readable for sparse matrices  {{and R's `Matrix` package uses a sophisticated version of this, as part of its `print()/show()` methods for (formally classed) sparse matrices}}.

Note that the documentation is not wrong strictly, as indeed, 
- by the time, `quote` is applied, all the numeric entries have become strings  and 
- it does not at all talk about `dimnames` (also in your example, we have a 1D array with dimnames, see `str(.)`):
```
> str(table(rep(c("", " ", "  "), 9:11)))
 'table' int [1:3(1d)] 9 10 11
 - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 1
  ..$ : chr [1:3] "" " " "  "
> 
``` 
but of course, it is *not* what you'd like to get here _and_
the documentation is not precise enough to become even misleading.

For back compatibility reasons, it'd be best to consider allowing  `quote = "dimnames"` (or equivalently `quote = "names"` )
or introduce a new optional argument, say `namesQuote = <logical>`  or  `namesQuote = <q-alike>)`  where in the latter case,
`dQuote(<names>, q = namesQuote)` would be called inside `print.table()`.
comments.creator: maechler
michaelchirico4
comments.text:
> For back compatibility reasons, it'd be best to consider allowing quote = "dimnames" (or equivalently quote = "names" )
or introduce a new optional argument, say namesQuote = <logical> or namesQuote = <q-alike>) where in the latter case,
dQuote(<names>, q = namesQuote) would be called inside print.table().

That makes sense to me, thanks.

Note to future self: I was confusing myself a bit about how I expected `quote=TRUE` to work based on how it works for data.table's `print()` method:

```
DT=data.table(a=1, ` `=2, c='', d = ' ')
print(DT, quote=TRUE)
#        "a"     " "      "c"      "d"
#    "<num>" "<num>" "<char>" "<char>"
# 1:     "1"     "2"       ""      " "
print(as.data.frame(DT), quote=TRUE)
#     a      c   d
# 1 "1" "2" "" " "
```

More generally, data.frame has the same issue cited for `table` objects here:

```
print(data.frame(` ` = 1, `  ` = 2, `   ` = 3, check.names=FALSE), quote=TRUE)
#              
# 1 "1" "2" "3"
```

So presumably whatever we do here for the table method could apply to the data.frame method, too.

About `print.data.frame()` specifically, the help says

>quote	
logical, indicating whether or not entries should be printed with surrounding quotes.

and does not put the column names in quotes whether empty or not.

However the `names()` does return an empty string. So I think that is the method to get names with the quoted empty strings.
comments.creator: elin.waring

comments.text:
Thanks Erin! I actually like the description in `?print.data.frame` much better.

Looking now, I think part of why `?print.table` struggles here is that it's in 'print.Rd' alongside the description of `print()` generically and the factor method for `print()`.

One idea for improvement here (of the documentation alone) is to move the description of the table method into 'print.dataframe.Rd', so that the two print methods of "tabular" data are together.

I can prepare a patch, but want to gauge interest first since it will require careful splicing.
